scope: Domain atomic deleteMany and unknown-state quarantine required by current Schedule management

paired.method: Actual fixed DomainImpl and Native over controlled backend units; FIFO decisions, backend call counts, listener snapshots/failures, rejection identity, quarantined reads/queued writes and close precedence.

verification.native: 22 passed: domain batch/quarantine, actual JSON one-publication/cold-reopen, current Schedule storage and domain route/lifecycle consumers.

behavior: deleteMany deduplicates and decides presence inside its FIFO slot, invokes one atomic backend batch, updates all in-memory rows before announcing individual changes, and returns the actual count. Empty batches make no backend call.

Ordinary backend failures preserve the domain view and permit later writes. StorageError unknown-state quarantines the domain with the original error identity, blocking reads and even already-queued writes before their backend calls.

Close drains the chain and releases once; after completed close the closed error takes precedence over a prior quarantine. Observer failures do not reject committed writes or suppress remaining notifications.
diagnostics: The first observer fixture used a global schema admitting null, which defineDomain correctly refused. The fixture now uses an integer schema; original failure/report remains retained.

cleanup.retained: Paired traces/errors, command/input hashes, logs/XML/Source results and compact observations. Owned short synthetic workspaces and isolated homes removed.

limitations: The atomic backend vocabulary has no sequential-delete fallback. Single JSON implements it; per-record JSON and SQLite implementations are separate pending provider work and are not certified here.
